audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 1, 2 and 3 read Tryndamere while the whys[] beside them say 'even farming', 'skill-based' and 'no clear favorite'.
audit.why: packet.levelChart gives Skill for rows 0-3, the mirror audit also gives Level 1 and Level 3 to Skill, and the page's own text agrees. Rows 0-2 are the subset where packet, mirror and text all point the same way.
audit.corrected: Levels 1, 2 and 3 set to Skill in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and 'dodge Rupture then trade while it's down' was sold as a large window.
audit.why: Rupture is 6s flat — the window is short and the advice needs to say so. Feral Scream is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s, Vorpal Spikes 8/7/6/5/4s, and Feast is 80/70/60s against your Undying Rage at 120s, so his ultimate comes back faster than yours.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d and mid carry Rupture's 6s; spikes[1].text carries the 80s-versus-120s ultimate comparison.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text claimed you are 'immune to it as an execute during ghost form'. Tryndamere has no ghost form and Undying Rage is not an immunity to a specific ability.
audit.why: Riot's text: he is unable to die no matter how wounded. What actually beats Feast is refusing to die during the window, not a form that does not exist.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text rewritten around Undying Rage refusing death and the ultimate cooldown gap.

audit.whatIsWrong: Feral Scream's silence was named in a don't title ('Get silenced mid-crit') but never explained anywhere, and Feast's true damage was never stated.
audit.why: The silence removes Spinning Slash — your only exit — for its duration, so the sequencing rule is to hold E until after the scream rather than opening with it. Feast is true damage, so armour is not the counter.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[1].d and mid state the silence and the hold-E rule; wants.foe[1] states the true damage.

edits.before: Cho'Gath hits 6 wanting Feast (R) as an execute, but with Undying Rage up you're immune to it as an execute during ghost form. Play for a level-6 all-in: full Fury, E in, W to slow his escape, and burst him before he can Rupture-Scream you off.
edits.after: Cho'Gath hits 6 wanting Feast as an execute, but Undying Rage refuses to die through it — his ult is 80s at rank 1 against your 120s, so spend yours only on his. Play the all-in: full Fury, E in, W to slow the escape, burst before Feral Scream lands.

edits.before: Through levels 3-6 it stays a skill matchup around dodging Rupture. If you eat his Q you take a bad trade; if you dodge it you get a free E-in crit while it's down. His level-6 Feast is scary but telegraphed, and once you hit 6 your Undying Rage flips the all-in in your favor.
edits.after: Through levels 3-6 it stays a skill matchup around dodging Rupture, and at 6s the window it leaves is short. Eat the Q and you take a bad trade; dodge it and you get a free E-in crit. Feral Scream silences you for its full duration, so hold Spinning Slash for the exit rather than opening with it.

edits.before: Telegraphed. E-spin out of it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Rupture is 6s and knocks up — clear the telegraph, then step in.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Feral Scream is 11s and silences — hold E for after it lands.

edits.before: Stack Feast size and health to become unkillable
edits.after: Stack Feast — true damage, so armour won't help

notes: Rows 3-6 of the chart are in direct conflict and I did not guess them: packet.levelChart gives Levels 4-5 to Skill and Level 6 / First item / 2+ items to Tryndamere, while the mirror audit's chart gives all four to Cho'Gath. The page's whys[4], whys[5] and whys[6] side with the packet. Raised as a question rather than resolved, since mirror-fix.js will overwrite whichever side is wrong and a guess here would flip four rows on a paying user's page.
